races.name: attheraces.com/marketmovers Handicap

runners_data.name: Bintkend
runners_data.note: Prominent racer well-placed tactically but lacks proven form at this level despite recent third place effort
runners_data.spotlight: Unexposed filly; did not live up to pedigree in her three qualifying races but kept on for third behind a fairly useful filly in a Wolverhampton maiden (9.4f, AW) in February and could have significant improvement to come in handicaps.

runners_data.name: A Major Payne
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer carrying penalty after Wednesday win but has fitness advantage and strong recent momentum
runners_data.comment: 0-17 but he's been in the first three on 11 occasions; holds solid claims once again
runners_data.spotlight: Placed three consecutive times before leading close home to open account at Nottingham (1m2f, good; front pair clear) on Wednesday, carries 5lb penalty here but should be fine on the forecast slower ground; ought to be right in the thick of things again.

runners_data.name: Bobacious
runners_data.note: Front-runner with clear tactical edge as sole pace-setter, recent course form suggests ready to capitalize
runners_data.comment: Finished last season on a downswing; sold for 1,000gns since; others more likely
runners_data.spotlight: Front-runner who gave good account when placed behind King's Hand over C&D (good) on last month's stable debut; that run came after a layoff and he remains on a good mark; handles good to soft (unraced on anything slower); no surprise if he makes a bold bid.

runners_data.name: King's Hand
runners_data.note: Hold-up style suits course but needs pace to develop, strong record here including January AW victory
runners_data.comment: Did well to score after a slow start at Lingfield ten days ago; respected under penalty
runners_data.spotlight: Signed off for Sir Mark Prescott with 1m2f AW win here in January and has performed well on all four starts for new stable, most notably when recovering from a slow start to win over C&D (1m2f, good) last month; still unexposed on turf but he often races too freely and is a bit of a character.

runners_data.name: Kokanee
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who hasn't progressed since Beverley win but went close at Pontefract last time
runners_data.spotlight: Yet to make any significant further progress since winning handicap debut at Beverley (1m2f, good) in spring 2025 but went close at Pontefract (1m, good to soft) two starts ago and should cope if the ground remains soft.

runners_data.name: Kaaranah
runners_data.note: Hold-up veteran boosted by cheekpieces with two recent Wolverhampton wins, wide Kempton trip last start
runners_data.comment: Resurgent 9yo who has won at Wolverhampton in his last two starts; big player again
runners_data.spotlight: Seemingly boosted by cheekpieces when winning twice at Wolverhampton (9.4f, AW) in April and endured a wide trip before keeping on steadily for sixth at Kempton (1m, AW; no headgear, as today) last month; versatile ground-wise on turf; can't be ignored.

runners_data.name: Birthday Angel
runners_data.note: Long absence and hold-up style create challenges, though low weight of 117lbs provides some compensation
runners_data.comment: Two hurdle wins last month, the latter over C&D; this race is much more competitive
runners_data.spotlight: Scored on the Flat at Brighton (1m2f, good to soft) in October and added two hurdle wins to his tally the following month; probably still on a workable Flat mark and seems versatile regarding ground but has fitness to prove after 172-day absence.

races.paceDynamic: Bobacious is the sole confirmed front-runner and will dictate proceedings from the outset, likely setting a sustainable gallop over this stamina-testing trip without early pressure. The remaining six runners all show prominent to hold-up tendencies, meaning Bobacious will get an easy lead through the early stages before the field closes up in the straight. With multiple hold-up horses including A Major Payne, King's Hand, Kokanee and Kaaranah needing to come from off the pace, this race shape strongly favours either the lone leader Bobacious or prominent racers like Bintkend who can track the pace without getting too far back. The tactical advantage clearly lies with horses that can race handily rather than those relying on late runs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Bobacious Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Bobacious maintains his front-running advantage without serious early challenges
scenarios.body: The veteran gets first run on his rivals and proves difficult to peg back, while the hold-up brigade leave themselves too much to do from off the steady pace. His recent placed effort behind King's Hand suggests he's primed for another big run when allowed to dictate.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: King's Hand Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens enough in the straight to set up King's Hand's finishing kick
scenarios.body: The four-year-old's proven course form and recovery ability come to the fore as he picks off Bobacious in the final furlong. His hold-up style benefits from any increased tempo that stretches the field.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: A Major Payne Follows Up
scenarios.trigger: If the penalty-carrying gelding handles the 5lb rise and gets a clear run
scenarios.body: His Wednesday Nottingham win gives him a fitness edge and confidence boost that outweighs the weight penalty. The hold-up style that served him well at Nottingham can work again if the pace is true.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Benefits From Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the principals get involved in pace battles or traffic problems
scenarios.body: Kaaranah or Birthday Angel capitalize on a muddling race where the favorites compromise each other. The cheekpieces continue to help Kaaranah while Birthday Angel's low weight becomes a factor.

watchPoints.text: Bobacious getting too easy a lead in the early stages as all six rivals are hold-up or prominent types
A Major Payne handling the 5lb penalty after his Wednesday Nottingham victory just three days ago
King's Hand finding clear racing room given his need to weave through traffic from off the pace
Kaaranah's cheekpieces continuing their positive effect after helping him win twice at Wolverhampton
The pace development in the back straight as multiple hold-up horses need to start making their moves

races.name: Buy A Share At daretodreamracing.co.uk Handicap

runners_data.name: Royal Bodyguard
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse facing lack of early pace, returned from layoff with encouraging third but faded late suggesting stamina/fitness concerns
runners_data.comment: Entitled to come on for his comeback and this is easier but he's vulnerable to improvers
runners_data.spotlight: Stepped up on reappearance when third of ten over 1m at Windsor (good to firm) a fortnight ago, although he faded inside the final furlong and this sometimes keen goer wouldn't be sure to benefit from this slightly longer distance.

runners_data.name: Sovereign Bay
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner with clear tactical advantage, caught eye on debut when denied room and gets ideal scenario with no pace pressure
runners_data.comment: Two backward steps since going close on debut; chance if tapping back into initial promise
runners_data.spotlight: Caught the eye (repeatedly denied a clear run) when keeping on late for fourth of 11 on 1m Haydock handicap and turf debut (good to soft) 15 days ago; possibly not entirely straightforward (has taken a keen hold on most starts) but it's likely he has the ability to win off this mark.

runners_data.name: Rajendra
runners_data.note: Hold-up type returning from 100-day break, needs strong pace to be effective but won't get it in this lineup
runners_data.comment: Promise on last month's return at Southwell (1m); more to come but improvement essential
runners_data.spotlight: Tough to argue his opening mark is generous on bare form but he's more than hinted at ability and appeals as a potential improver back from a 100-day break.

runners_data.name: Daretobedifferent
runners_data.note: Prominent racer carrying 6lb penalty for recent Nottingham win, well-positioned tactically to track the leader
runners_data.comment: 0-11 but good runs on her last two starts and unexposed as a miler; each-way shout again
runners_data.spotlight: Came good at the 12th time of asking when seeing off six rivals at Nottingham (extended 1m, good) last Sunday; not obviously well treated under a 6lb penalty.

runners_data.name: Del Corso
runners_data.note: Prominent style suits race shape, consistent spring form suggests he's found his level in handicaps
runners_data.spotlight: Third around 1m at Nottingham (good) and Yarmouth (good to firm) switched to handicaps this spring; below the level of those efforts on soft ground last year but it was his debut; has a useful pedigree and too soon to suggest he's reached his limit.

runners_data.name: Fans Favourite
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with 5lb claimer, showed improvement last time but needs pace collapse to feature
runners_data.comment: Not particularly solid on 2yo form; makes reappearance
runners_data.spotlight: Showed he can be competitive in handicaps at the second attempt when returning from five months off to finish third of 14 over 1m at Windsor 12 days ago; raced only on good/good to firm on turf; claims with Mason Paetel taking a handy 5lb off.

runners_data.name: Takeitorleaveit
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with 7lb claimer aboard, proven soft ground form gives him claims if pace sets up right
runners_data.comment: Record of 141, all at Bath, since handicapping; one of the stronger contenders on form
runners_data.spotlight: Winner over 1m at Bath on soft last autumn and returned to the same venue to double his tally on reappearance (good to firm); a wide trip provides a possible excuse for a lesser effort at Windsor since (Fans Favourite ahead of him).

races.paceDynamic: Sovereign Bay will set the pace from the front with minimal pressure, as he's the only confirmed early leader in this small field. Daretobedifferent, Del Corso, and Takeitorleaveit will track in behind, but none are aggressive pace-pressers. The lack of early speed means Sovereign Bay can dictate fractions and kick for home when ready, while hold-up horses Royal Bodyguard, Rajendra, and Fans Favourite will need the pace to collapse to get competitive. This controlled tempo strongly favours prominent racers and the pace-setter.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sovereign Bay Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Sovereign Bay maintains an uncontested lead through steady fractions
scenarios.body: He can quicken off manageable pace and prove hard to peg back, while prominent trackers get first run on any faltering. Hold-up horses face an impossible task without pace collapse.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Surge Succeeds
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace proves too slow and the field bunches turning in
scenarios.body: Hold-up horses get their chance as the race becomes a sprint finish, with Royal Bodyguard's class telling. The front-runners may pay for their earlier exertions.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Sovereign Bay sets it up perfectly but one tracker times their move better
scenarios.body: Daretobedifferent or Del Corso can use the ideal pace setup to strike late and collar the leader. The pace-setter does the donkey work but gets passed close home.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Sovereign Bay goes too slow early then gets swamped by multiple challengers
scenarios.body: The race becomes messy with horses coming from everywhere, creating opportunities for unconsidered runners. Form lines get thrown out in the scramble finish.

watchPoints.text: Sovereign Bay dictating splits - if he gets easy lead and kicks clear turning in, he'll be very hard to catch
Royal Bodyguard's position at halfway - if too far back on modest pace, his class won't matter
How aggressively the prominent trackers position - if they sit too far off Sovereign Bay, they hand him race
Pace through first half-mile - anything slower than moderate completely rules out hold-up horses
Daretobedifferent under penalty - whether 6lb burden affects his ability to track and challenge the leader

races.name: Free Bets On attheraces.com Restricted Maiden Stakes (Bands C And D) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Liberate
runners_data.spotlight: Fifth foal; half-brother to French winners Chandler's Song (1m1f) and Woodwind (1m/9.5f); dam 7f/1m winner (RPR 93); his in-form trainer can ready one first time and the betting could be informative on debut.

runners_data.name: Parc Dosne
runners_data.spotlight: 4,000euros yearling, resold 30,000euros yearling; second foal; half-brother to 1m/1m2f winner Quai De Bethune (RPR 107); dam unraced, out of half-sister to French 1,000 Guineas/Coronation Stakes winner Ervedya; with a respected trainer (who also saddles Relentless Hero); could go well on debut.

runners_data.name: Celestial Cen
runners_data.spotlight: 2,000euros 3yo; fifth foal; half-sister to US 7f dirt 2yo winner Golden Sights (RPR 93); dam US stakes-placed 5.5f turf 2yo winner, half-sister to US 8.5f Grade 1 winner; in good hands and the betting should guide on debut; trainer also saddles the once-raced Fabled Spirit.

runners_data.name: Cherringham
runners_data.spotlight: Sixth foal; sister to 1m2f winner Mighty Quiet (RPR 78), half-sister to winners Silent City (1m; 88) and Maurice Dancer (7f AW 2yo; 69); dam from family of top miler Soviet Song who raced in these colours; newcomer from a powerful yard and the standard set isn't overly daunting; interesting.

runners_data.name: Fabled Spirit
runners_data.comment: Likeable pedigree and in good hands; a market check is advised on debut
runners_data.spotlight: Ran green throughout and always behind on recent debut at Leicester (1m2f, good to firm); however, there's potential in his pedigree and he was backed in to 11-1; trainer also saddles the newcomer Celestial Cen; interesting to see how he goes in the betting this time.

runners_data.name: Cold Fish
runners_data.comment: Promising third at Chelmsford in December and could be dangerous if he can build on that
runners_data.spotlight: Third on debut at Chelmsford (1m2f, AW) last December and again showed promise when occupying the same position at Goodwood (1m, good) last month; shaped last time as though the return to 1m2f would suit; leading player.

runners_data.name: Probation
runners_data.spotlight: He hasn't threatened on his first two starts (9.4f/1m2f, AW/good to firm) but has shown promise and made the frame on each occasion; open to improvement and could be in the shake-up.

runners_data.name: Ataturk
runners_data.spotlight: Well beaten at big odds at Newbury on both starts (1m/1m2f, soft/good) and this half-brother to connections' smart stayer Kyle Of Lochalsh will be of greater interest when stepped up in trip in handicaps.

runners_data.name: Relentless Hero
runners_data.comment: Ability on both starts; improvement needed but could take step forward at some point
runners_data.spotlight: He's shown ability on all three starts, most recently beaten just under 3l when a front-running fourth of 12 at Leicester (1m2f, good to firm; unraced on softer); he's one to consider.

races.name: Free Race Replays On attheraces.com Handicap

runners_data.name: Zoustar Dreams
runners_data.note: Fresh cheekpieces helped at Catterick but faces a quick turnaround and needs strong pace to set up her hold-up style.
runners_data.comment: 0-7 and better form on AW so far; workable mark and headgear back on but need to see more.
runners_data.spotlight: Fresh cheekpieces may have helped when she took advantage of a reduced mark to open her account at Catterick (6f, good to firm) one week ago; up 6lb but started quickly to make all that day so has to be feared with the potential to bag the favoured stands' rail if clearing Jane Of The Jungle; yet to be tested on ground worse than good but her dam recorded best effort on soft.

runners_data.name: Rosieisme Darling
runners_data.note: Untried on soft ground but her prominent style suits this race shape and she showed good form at Windsor last time.
runners_data.spotlight: Untried on softer than good ground; three runs on turf and the best of them came last time out when third of 12 at Windsor (6f, good) 19 days ago; was mucked about that day and this dual 5f AW winner should be fine back down in trip, especially given a likely good gallop despite the small field.

runners_data.name: Jane Of The Jungle
runners_data.note: Natural leader who can control tempo but recent form suggests she needs everything to fall right from the front.
runners_data.comment: Fourth of five in blanket finish over 5f last Thursday; stays 6f and can't be ruled out
runners_data.spotlight: Another front-runner who was involved in a blanket finish when fourth behind dead-heater My Mate Mackley at Chepstow (5f, good to soft) on her penultimate start; not so good at 6f eight days ago but a sharp break could put her in pole position to bag the rail.

runners_data.name: My Mate Mackley
runners_data.note: Gelding operation sparked improvement at Chepstow but his hold-up style needs a strong gallop to be effective.
runners_data.spotlight: Gelded ahead of his handicap debut and it was a good step forward when on the pace before sharing the spoils at Chepstow (5f, good to soft; Jane Of The Jungle fourth) 16 days ago; that was his first go at this trip and the handicapper could only dish out a 1lb nudge to this unexposed sprinter.

races.paceDynamic: Jane Of The Jungle is the sole confirmed front-runner in this small field and will likely dictate terms from the outset without serious early pressure. Rosieisme Darling may track in second, while both hold-up horses Zoustar Dreams and My Mate Mackley will need the pace to be strong enough to set up their finishing kicks. With only one natural leader over this sprint distance, Jane Of The Jungle can control the tempo and make it difficult for the closers to reel her in. This race shape strongly favours prominent runners who can sit close to the pace and kick, as the tempo may not be strong enough to fully expose the leader.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Front Running
scenarios.trigger: If Jane Of The Jungle gets an easy lead and dictates moderate fractions
scenarios.body: She can string out the field and prove hard to peg back with Rosieisme Darling best placed to strike from second. The hold-up horses face an uphill task if the pace isn't strong enough to bring them into play.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Takeover
scenarios.trigger: If Rosieisme Darling pressures Jane Of The Jungle early or takes closer order
scenarios.body: The extra pace helps set up a more tactical finish where the Windsor third can use her class edge. Jane Of The Jungle may weaken if pressed throughout the early stages.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Charge Success
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is strong enough between Jane Of The Jungle and Rosieisme Darling
scenarios.body: Zoustar Dreams can reproduce her Catterick win with the cheekpieces still on and benefit from a strong gallop. My Mate Mackley showed improved form when gelded and could also capitalize on a hot pace.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Stalemate
scenarios.trigger: If Jane Of The Jungle goes too slowly early and the field bunches up turning for home
scenarios.body: A messy sprint finish develops where any horse can win depending on luck in running. The race becomes more about positioning than running style with gaps and interference crucial.

watchPoints.text: Jane Of The Jungle breaks slowly or gets pressured early as she needs to establish position to be effective
Rosieisme Darling handles the softer ground on debut as she's untried on anything slower than good
Zoustar Dreams shows early pace despite her hold-up rating as she may need to be closer in a small field
My Mate Mackley gets cover early as he showed at Chepstow that prominent tactics can work better than waiting
The pace after the first furlong develops as Jane Of The Jungle may go too slowly if unchallenged

races.name: Free Tips On attheraces.com Restricted Maiden Stakes (Bands C And D) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Princess Maitha
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with proven soft ground form returning from 318-day absence, holds clear class advantage
runners_data.spotlight: Well-bred filly who made a promising debut for Charlie Johnston when clear second to useful rival at Catterick (7f, soft) last summer; not seen since but has a good draw for this stable debut; leading contender.

runners_data.name: Nothing But Love
runners_data.note: Unknown quantity making debut but strong pedigree suggests stamina for hold-up tactics
runners_data.spotlight: 1,000gns 2yo; second foal; half-sister to 1m2f winner Approval (RPR 97); dam unraced half-sister to winners Ehtiraas (1m) and Saraha (1m4f AW); hooded for belated debut; seems unlikely to meet the standard required.

runners_data.name: Dovecote
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who faded on debut but gelding operation may have improved attitude
runners_data.spotlight: In good hands and has a good pedigree but struggled to get competitive on debut at Chelmsford (7f, AW) in November; gelded in February; needs to be a completely different proposition today.

runners_data.name: Call Alert
runners_data.note: Unraced debutant drawn wide with stamina pedigree but completely unknown ability
runners_data.spotlight: Fourth foal; dam 11.6f/1m4f winner (RPR 88), half-sister to prolific 6f-1m4f winner Spiritual Air; drawn on the wing for this debut run; considered only if lively in the betting.

runners_data.name: Show Me Gold
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent runner with solid AW form though turf debut creates question marks
runners_data.comment: Went close at Wolverhampton on debut last month and could have a significant part to play
runners_data.spotlight: Runner-up on both AW starts, latterly in 13-runner maiden at Kempton (7f) in January; that form isn't anything to get too excited about but she has a big role to play here if suited by the switch to turf.

runners_data.name: Vicit Venture
runners_data.note: Hold-up type prone to fading who lacks the class for this level of competition
runners_data.comment: Soundly beaten on Southwell AW debut (7f); lots to find dropped to 6f; hood discarded
runners_data.spotlight: Not disgraced when eighth of 12 at Windsor (6f, good to firm) last month, his second start, but makes limited appeal here.

runners_data.name: Drymee
runners_data.note: Prominent performer who disappointed last time but showed early promise and suits trip
runners_data.comment: Promising debut fourth at Leicester in September for Joseph Parr; open to progress
runners_data.spotlight: Belied 150-1 odds when promising fourth for Joseph Parr at Leicester (7f, good) in September but, having been gelded, was disappointing when weakening seventh of nine for new stable (same owners) at Kempton (7f, AW) last month; needs that recent outing to have brought her on.

runners_data.name: Ernie McCrew
runners_data.note: Limited prominent runner whose recent efforts suggest handicaps more suitable
runners_data.comment: Hinted at ability when behind Vidmiyr on his debut at Wolverhampon; may be one for later
runners_data.spotlight: Not beaten that far on either appearance this spring (7f, AW/turf) but low-grade handicaps are probably next on his agenda.

runners_data.name: Mr Jeffrey
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with poor form who has shown nothing to suggest competitiveness
runners_data.comment: 300-1, beaten over 30l on Kempton AW (7f) 11 days ago
runners_data.spotlight: Well beaten at huge odds on both starts this spring (7f/6f); impossible to recommend.

runners_data.name: Don Pablo Colina
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with recent AW promise but needs to prove turf effectiveness
runners_data.comment: 125-1 for recent 1m debut on AW and dropped out; trip query at 7f; handicaps soon
runners_data.spotlight: Displayed promise when midfield on both AW starts last month (1m/7f) but will probably be of greater interest when switched to run-of-the-mill handicaps.

runners_data.name: Turton
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with modest form who ran just six days ago at Nottingham
runners_data.comment: 14-1 and never dangerous after a slow start on last month's debut (7f, AW); gelded since
runners_data.spotlight: Safely held on both starts, more recently when sixth of seven at Nottingham (8.3f, good) on Sunday; needs to take a big step forward.

runners_data.name: Arc At Her
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with minimal ability who likely needs longer trips to be effective
runners_data.comment: Last of nine on debut at Goodwood 16 days ago; lots to find.
runners_data.spotlight: Showed nothing more than minor promise on her two starts last month (1m/8.3f) and, judged on pedigree, she'll probably need longer trips to be seen to best effect.

runners_data.name: Sayidah Aleen
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who improved markedly when fitted with cheekpieces for new stable connections
runners_data.comment: Bought for 15,500gns since finishing last of four on debut; cheekpieces on for yard debut
runners_data.spotlight: Last of four on debut for Jack Channon (8.6f, AW) in March but seemingly aided by cheekpieces when keeping-on second (no threat to winner) for new stable here (7f, good) last month; each-way claims at least from a favourable draw.

races.paceDynamic: Princess Maitha and Show Me Gold will likely set a modest early pace from the front, with Drymee and Ernie McCrew tracking just behind in prominent positions. The sustained gallop will be manageable rather than fierce with only these limited pace-setters in a 13-runner field. The combination of soft ground and 7½f trip will create stamina-sapping conditions where horses need to stay on strongly through the final two furlongs. This race shape clearly favours prominent racers and hold-up horses with stamina reserves, penalising those who typically fade in the finish.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sustained Pace Grind
scenarios.trigger: If Princess Maitha and Show Me Gold maintain steady fractions without collapse
scenarios.body: The even tempo allows hold-up horses to close effectively while punishing those with finishing limitations. Stamina becomes the decisive factor on testing ground over this intermediate trip.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Benefits
scenarios.trigger: If the early leaders go too slowly and create a sprint finish
scenarios.body: Late-running horses get perfect conditions to unleash their turn of foot despite the soft ground. The lack of early pressure sets up a bunched finish where class tells.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Domination
scenarios.trigger: If Show Me Gold or Drymee press Princess Maitha from the outset
scenarios.body: The increased early pace stretches the field and creates gaps for the pace-setters to exploit. Horses tracking the speed gain tactical advantage over hold-up types.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Soft Ground Carnage
scenarios.trigger: If multiple horses struggle badly with the testing conditions
scenarios.body: The race becomes a war of attrition where proven soft ground performers gain significant advantage. Form lines become less relevant than ground conditions.

watchPoints.text: Princess Maitha's 318-day layoff could blunt her fitness despite her clear class advantage in this field
Nothing But Love's market support will reveal connections' confidence in this well-bred but unraced performer
Show Me Gold's turf debut effectiveness remains unproven despite consistent AW form this year
Dovecote's post-gelding improvement could transform his competitiveness after disappointing on debut
The early pace battle between Princess Maitha and Show Me Gold will determine the tactical setup for closers

races.name: Eikon Helping Young People In Surrey Handicap

runners_data.name: Pixie Diva
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with strong AW form but 0-5 on turf, though showed promise when third at Thirsk over 5f on good ground
runners_data.comment: Lightly raced; just 1lb higher than for Newcastle win in March; not ruled out
runners_data.spotlight: Dual sprint winner on AW; 0-5 on turf but ran well when favourite for big-field event at Thirsk (5f, good; finished 1l third) most recently; warrants respect off same mark.

runners_data.name: Monsieur Kodi
runners_data.note: Prominent racer using 3lb claimer, failed to follow up February win but consistent turf performer with 1W4P on similar going
runners_data.comment: Banging at the door prior to Lingfield win (7f); had few chances in this headgear
runners_data.spotlight: Failed to back up the form of his February win last time, kept to 7f on AW; multiple sprint winner on turf and made the frame in last four attempts in this sphere; solid.

runners_data.name: Brazen Idol
runners_data.note: Hold-up type returning to turf after 66-day break, hasn't raced on grass for over two years which raises fitness concerns
runners_data.spotlight: Missed 2025; failed to back up reappearance effort last time, kept to Kempton AW; effective on turf in the past but hasn't raced in this sphere for over two years.

runners_data.name: Queue Dos
runners_data.note: Front-runner with 5lb apprentice claim, winless on turf (0-12) but showed decent form at Bath recently over similar trip
runners_data.comment: Four-time AW winner but she's 0-11 on turf and has been quiet in both runs this season
runners_data.spotlight: Four AW wins; 0-12 on turf but has largely consistent form in this sphere, creditable third at Bath (5.7f, good to firm) most recently; each-way possibilities.

runners_data.name: Charlie Mason
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner for in-form Tony Carroll stable (8/45 last 14 days), generally consistent with versatile surface form reading 222 off current mark
runners_data.comment: Usually a reliable sort whose five wins have all been over 6f; should run well.
runners_data.spotlight: Modest strike-rate in the last 14 months but he is generally consistent and is versatile as regards surfaces; form figures off current mark read 222; could go one better, with Myla Coppins taking off 7lb.

runners_data.name: Hierarchy
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with headgear changes (tongue-tie, blinkers), inconsistent 2026 AW form and hasn't won on turf since 2023
runners_data.comment: Below his best since winning at Lingfield in February and best watched.
runners_data.spotlight: Inconsistent on AW this year, aside from winning in February; well treated on best turf form but hasn't scored in this sphere since 2023.

runners_data.name: Tyger Bay

runners_data.spotlight: Far from solid on 2026 AW form, notwithstanding a March win, and rarely seen on turf in the last two years; others preferred.

runners_data.name: Raffles Angel

races.paceDynamic: Queue Dos will lead from the gates with Monsieur Kodi and Raffles Angel likely to press him early, creating a modest gallop over this 6f trip on soft ground. The majority of the field (Pixie Diva, Brazen Idol, Charlie Mason, Hierarchy, Tyger Bay) are hold-up types who will track the pace and rely on late finishing kicks. With soft conditions likely to emphasize stamina over pure speed and most runners preferring to come from behind, this setup strongly favors prominent racers and those with tactical speed who can position close to the pace without getting involved in early scrimmaging.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sustainable Pace Setup
scenarios.trigger: If Queue Dos leads uncontested and sets a steady tempo with minimal early pressure
scenarios.body: The soft ground and modest gallop will suit horses that can track the leaders without expending energy, allowing them to finish strongly when the field spreads out in the final furlong. Monsieur Kodi and Raffles Angel are perfectly positioned to capitalize on this tactical advantage.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes genuinely strong with sustained pressure between the front three
scenarios.body: The combination of soft ground and a strong gallop will set up perfectly for the back-markers to produce their trademark finishing kicks. Pixie Diva and Charlie Mason will benefit most from a truly-run race that stretches the field.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Queue Dos Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Queue Dos faces minimal early pressure and kicks clear approaching the final furlong
scenarios.body: His front-running style combined with the apprentice's 5lb claim could prove decisive if he can dictate terms throughout. The soft ground will test stamina reserves of those trying to reel him in from behind.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Finish
scenarios.trigger: If early leaders go too fast and multiple horses tie up in the soft conditions
scenarios.body: A slowly-run race that becomes a sprint finish will heavily favor the strongest finishers regardless of early position. Charlie Mason and Pixie Diva possess the turn of foot to capitalize on a tactical finish.

races.paceDynamic: Zambezi Diamond will set the pace from the front with minimal early pressure, as the only confirmed leader in this field. Beau Jardine, Kessaar Power and Daddy Chill will race prominently behind the leader, but none are aggressive enough to seriously challenge early. This creates a sustainable gallop that allows Zambezi Diamond to control fractions through the middle stages before the field closes late. The lack of pace pressure and gentle early gallop strongly favours hold-up horses who can finish from off the pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sustainable Pace Benefits Closers
scenarios.trigger: If Zambezi Diamond sets uncontested fractions and the pace stays moderate
scenarios.body: The gentle gallop allows hold-up horses to conserve energy and deliver strong finishing kicks. Late runners get ideal positioning as the field compresses in the straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Stays Strong
scenarios.trigger: If Zambezi Diamond maintains his recent improved form and gets easy lead
scenarios.body: The leader builds a decisive advantage through soft fractions and has enough left to resist late challenges. His recent fourth at long odds suggests untapped ability.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Beau Jardine or Kessaar Power track the leader perfectly and kick clear
scenarios.body: The prominent horses get ideal trips sitting just off the pace and have enough tactical speed to win the race. They avoid traffic problems that could hinder the hold-up brigade.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes extremely slow creating a messy sprint finish
scenarios.body: The lack of genuine early speed results in a bunched field and a chaotic final furlong. Any horse with a turn of foot regardless of position can capitalize.
